requirement: Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read` for this operation.
rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.fn` has one obligation. Criterion code uses `ValidationContext.read` for the read-node operation. That obligation concerns the Rust function binding, and `ValidationContext.read` is the cited context. The cited text says `read` returns the node contents or the domain error, and records the fingerprint of the returned contents.

The marked test is `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/validation.rs#fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]`. It calls `ValidationContext::read(&1)` directly on both an empty string and a large multi-byte Unicode string. It asserts the following:
- The returned contents format back to the original.
- The contents stay unchanged after the underlying graph is mutated.
- `dependencies()` is exactly `Dependency::Node(1, fp(original))`, so the fingerprint is recorded.
- A failed `read(&9)` returns the domain error `"missing"` and records no dependencies.
- The finished record is stale after the node changes.

The test covers the cited `ValidationContext.read` behavior in the subject's case, and it asserts outcomes rather than only running the code. The implementation is a single `fn[read]` site, and I found no further modes or boundaries in the requirement text that need separate tests. The behavior and inputs requirements that refine this operation carry their own test references.

:::{req} read_node.fn
Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read` for this operation.
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
